problems.title: Distance/similarity terminology does not establish a selection failure
problems.source_location: Section 4.3, PDF p.5; cited DEITA compute_distance/filter
claim: The sentence calls \(d\) nearest-neighbor cosine distance and accepts \(d<0.9\).
analysis: Literal standard distance \(1-\cos\) accepts a duplicate of \(e_1\) with distance \(0\), rejecting \(e_2\) and \(-e_1\) at distances \(1,2\). However, the cited DEITA implementation names a normalized dot product “distance” and rejects similarity above its threshold. It therefore excludes the duplicate and supplies a plausible inherited convention. Similarity \(c<0.9\) is equivalent to nearest distance \(d_{\min}>0.1\), not \(d_{\min}>0.9\); DEITA’s equality-retaining convention instead uses \(c\le0.9\).
result: Scope/terminology clarification only. The unavailable PhysHPO selector is not shown to use the literal reversed interpretation; no actual dataset or benchmark failure follows.
